text:
IncidentBot: INCIDENT created at 2026-03-14T22:34Z — KV cache pressure in us-west-2 serving pool. SLOs breaching (p95/p99), streaming stalls observed. Opening thread for live mitigation. Dashboard: https://ops.redwood.internal/incidents/6298765432 

Mia R: seeing p95 ~1.1s -> 900ms? wait updated graphs: p95 jumped to ~1.1s, p99 ~3.4s for generate endpoints in us-west-2. Streaming tail stalls: some streams stuck >10s. Correlating with high prefill activity and elevated eviction rates.

Jordan K: oncall (22:36Z). grabbing perf graphs. @Alex P can you paste prefill vs decode queue metrics?

Alex P: prefill queue length ~820 (normal <150). decode worker backlog ~120 (normal ~300) — decode looks underloaded relative to prefill. eviction-rate spiked x4 in last 6m. slab free fragments rising. this smells like prefill flooding small KV entries -> fragmentation + eviction thrashing.

Samir V: yup. prefill vs decode imbalance. quick mitigation options: throttle prefill producers for non-critical tenants, temporarily disable prefill for 'large-context' customer group, increase slab_compact_threshold to avoid immediate evictions.

Mia R: customer-impact summary: approx 2.7% of requests see >p99; most affected are long-context streaming sessions and batch embed jobs. No widespread 5xxs, but user-facing latency for interactive apps is bad.

SRE Bot: Auto-scaler action: +3 decode pods, +2 prefill pods in us-west-2 at 22:38Z (requested to relieve backlog).

Jordan K: executing live mitigations now: 1) throttle prefill producers for non-prod & guest tenants, 2) flip admin flag to force-decode fallback on streaming endpoints, 3) increase hot-key TTLs where safe. Will run canary changes first.

Alex P: applying admin toggles — putting commands here for audit:
```bash
# throttle prefill via control-plane
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/flags -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -d '{"prefill_throttle_pct":40, "scope":"guest,nonprod"}'
# enable force-decode route for streaming
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/routes/streaming -d '{"force_decode":true, "scope":"us-west-2"}'
# scale decode pods (k8s)
kubectl -n inference scale deploy/decode-workers --replicas=30 --context=us-west-2
```

Samir V: note: force-decode increases CPU but reduces KV churn since we skip prefill writes. Expect some cost increase but should reduce fragmentation quickly.

Mia R: after throttle & force-decode canary (10% traffic) — p95 down from 1.1s -> 720ms, p99 from 3.4s -> 1.9s on canary subset. Good sign but cluster-wide p99 still elevated ~2.8s. eviction rate down ~30% on canary nodes.

Jordan K: good. next step: schedule slab compaction and a controlled restart of a subset of prefill workers to trigger slab reuse. This is invasive (may cause short blips) — propose target one shard pair at a time. Samir, can you prepare defrag job?

Samir V: preparing `kv-slab-defrag` job. plan: drain one prefill node pair, run compaction, restart prefill pods on pair, bring back in. roll through 3 pairs over 30m. Command (dry-run shown):
```bash
kubectl -n infra exec job/kv-slab-defrag -- /bin/defrag --shard-pair=shard-7 --dry-run
# to run for real once approved:
# kubectl -n infra exec job/kv-slab-defrag -- /bin/defrag --shard-pair=shard-7 --force
```

Alex P: also suggest a short-term routing change: shift 10% of streaming traffic to quantized/alt model variant that has smaller KV footprint. Reduced cache pressure on main pool. I'll open a rollout.

Mia R: agreed. route 10% now, monitor. Also dropping long-tail batch priority for 20m to reduce prefill burst.

SRE Bot: Canary rollout for force-decode (10%) successful at 22:52Z. Telemetry: canary p99 -> 1.9s, eviction-rate -30% on canary nodes.

Jordan K: initiating slab compaction on one pair now (shard-7). Running during low-traffic window but this will cause ~1-3s stalls for affected requests. notifying downstream teams.

Eva L: (on standby) if compaction causes regressions we should rollback prefill toggle & re-route traffic to fallback model immediately. Also be ready to pause compaction.

Mia R: compaction started. watching metrics.

Alex P: after compaction shard-7: local fragmentation % down 42%. p99 on that shard's local traffic down to 1.1s. cluster-wide p99 dropping to 2.2s. good.

Jordan K: continuing roll through shard pairs. current mitigations in effect: prefill_throttle=40% for guest/nonprod, force-decode enabled (global for streaming), 10% traffic shifted to quantized model, slab compaction rolling.

Samir V: long-term fixes to prevent recurrence: 1) enforce backpressure at prefill producer side (reject when decode lag < threshold), 2) smarter slab allocator to avoid small-key fragmentation, 3) limit prefill write amplification from batch embed jobs. I'll create follow-up tickets.

Mia R: customer comms note: engineering investigating; some customers may see slower streams. mitigation in progress. No action required from support unless customers file severity tickets.

Jordan K: Summary for handoff -> Night oncall (Eva L):
- Incident: KV cache pressure -> p95/p99 latency spikes + streaming stalls in us-west-2.
- Root cause (working hypothesis): prefill vs decode imbalance causing slab fragmentation and eviction thrash.
- Mitigations applied: prefill throttle (guest/nonprod 40%), force-decode enabled for streaming, route 10% to quantized model, slab compaction rolling across shard pairs.
- Current state: compaction 1/3 done, cluster p99 improving ~2.2s -> trending down. eviction-rate decreasing.
- Customer impact: ~2.7% requests > p99, mostly long-context streaming and batch embed jobs. No mass 5xx.
- Runbook links: https://docs.redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-fragmentation, https://ops.redwood.internal/playbooks/slab-defrag
- Commands used (audit): see earlier curl/kubectl snippets in thread.
- Next steps for night: finish compaction roll, monitor p99/p95 & streaming stall counts, be ready to rollback force-decode if CPU skyrockets or customer regressions.

Jordan K: handing off to @Eva L now. I'm available via DM for quick questions. 

Eva L: taking over at 23:12Z. I have the checklist. will watch chest telemetry and alerts. ping me if latency goes back up or if compaction causes >5% errors.

IncidentBot: INCIDENT status updated: mitigations applied, monitoring. Incident severity downgraded to SEV-2 at 23:20Z pending full recovery.

Eva L: noted. I'll post another update if we finish compaction roll or if rollback needed.
